title: acs run state (runs/<run-id>/run.json)
description: The RUN machine (§4.3): one workflow's progress over one subject. Replaces pipeline-state.json. `steps` is OPEN -- the 18-name enum is gone, because step names validate against the RESOLVED WORKFLOW and skill/leg names against the SKILL DIRECTORIES, while this schema validates shape only. That is what makes a new workflow a YAML file and a new skill a directory, neither touching a schema. `skipped` and `handed_off` are absent from the status enums by design: the first recorded a workflow predicate's answer (a step with nothing to do is `completed` with an `outcome`), the second named a reason rather than a state (it is now `interrupted` plus `stop_reason`).

workflow.description: The workflow's file name without its extension. There is no `name:` key in a workflow -- the file IS the name.

cursor.description: The first step in workflow order that is not completed, or null when every step is. With no needs: graph there is no ready-set to compute -- this is the whole of 'what runs next'.

steps.description: {step-name: entry}. Keyed by SKILL NAME: with no id: in a workflow, a step IS a skill. A step absent from here is pending.

loops.description: {step-name: {iteration, max}} for each loop the workflow declares.

subject.description: What this run is about. A ticket id, when supplied, is the run's SUBJECT and never its partition name -- which is what lets a run start from a bare prompt.

outcome.description: Why this step completed, when it completes in more than one way. The vocabulary is the skill's own, in skills/<name>/state.schema.json. A FAILURE is never an outcome -- that is `status: failed`.

leg.description: The leg an entry point dispatched to, e.g. code-standard for the code step.
